text: Iranian forces seized a UK-flagged tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz amid rising tension over sanctions enforcement.
Iranian officials publicly threatened to close the Strait of Hormuz to all shipping if the country's own oil exports were blocked by sanctions.
The US ended sanctions waivers for countries importing Iranian crude, escalating the standoff around Gulf shipping lanes.
Two tankers were attacked in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz; Gulf states raised naval alert levels in response.
Iran conducted naval exercises near the Strait of Hormuz and reiterated its ability to close the strait in response to further sanctions.
Houthi forces began targeting commercial vessels in the southern Red Sea approach to the Suez Canal, citing the Gaza conflict.
Houthi forces claimed a missile and drone attack on three commercial vessels in the Red Sea in a single day, marking a sharp escalation from earlier isolated incidents.
BP announced a temporary pause of all Red Sea oil transits following renewed Houthi attacks, becoming the first major oil company to publicly halt transits through the corridor.
US and UK forces conducted air strikes against Houthi missile and radar sites in Yemen in direct response to the escalating shipping attacks.
Multiple major shipping lines announced rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope rather than transiting the Red Sea, citing attack risk.
War-risk insurance premiums for Red Sea transits rose sharply, reported in the range of 1-2% of vessel value versus a pre-crisis baseline near 0.1%.
A container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days, halting an estimated $9 billion/day of transiting trade.
A Houthi missile strike sank a bulk carrier in the Red Sea, the first vessel loss of the campaign against shipping in the corridor.
The US and allies moved to restrict imports of Russian-origin crude, redirecting some Atlantic-basin supply flows.
OPEC+ producers, several with Atlantic-basin export terminals, adjusted output quotas, with muted effect on shipping-lane risk.
A hurricane forced temporary closure of several US Gulf Coast export terminals feeding Atlantic crude routes.
A Russia-Saudi production dispute triggered a sharp oil price collapse, with no direct shipping-lane disruption reported.
The US sanctioned a major Atlantic-basin state oil company, disrupting some crude export financing without closing shipping lanes.
A regional piracy-reporting center logged a rise in small-tanker hijackings for fuel theft in the Malacca Strait approaches.
Port congestion and COVID-related crew-change restrictions slowed tanker transits through the Malacca Strait.
Littoral states expanded joint naval patrols in the Malacca Strait following a multi-year rise in reported piracy incidents.
Malacca Strait tanker traffic reached a multi-year high as Asia-Pacific refiners increased throughput, with no security incidents reported.
A tanker ran aground in the Malacca Strait's shallow traffic separation scheme, briefly disrupting transit scheduling.
